concepts.title: Landfill Disposal
concepts.definition: A designated low-lying open area where city garbage is dumped, flattened, and eventually covered with a layer of soil.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Repurposing waste dumping grounds into public parks or playgrounds after they are full.
question_patterns: what is a landfill
how is garbage disposed of in a landfill
what happens to a landfill after it is completely filled
describe the process of managing non-useful garbage components

solution_steps.explain: Identify and separate the non-useful components of garbage from the reusable ones.
Spread the non-useful waste over the low-lying landfill area.
Apply a layer of soil over the spread garbage to cover it.

concepts.title: Composting
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, the action of converting organic wastes like kitchen scraps and plant remains into nutrient-rich manure through natural decomposition.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Turning biodegradable waste into useful manure for plants.
question_patterns: define composting
how is manure formed from garbage
what kind of waste is suitable for making compost
explain the conversion of kitchen waste into manure

solution_steps.explain: Gather organic materials like fruit peels, vegetable scraps, and dry leaves.
Place the organic waste in a pit and cover it with soil.
Allow the material to rot over time until it turns into a black, smell-free substance.

concepts.title: Waste Segregation (Blue and Green Bins)
concepts.definition: The practice of sorting garbage into separate containers based on whether they are recyclable or biodegradable.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, Separating materials that rot from those that do not to improve waste management.
question_patterns: why are there blue and green bins
what goes into a blue dustbin
what goes into a green dustbin
explain the importance of separating waste at the source

solution_steps.explain: Identify if the waste is organic (kitchen/plant) or inorganic (plastic/glass/metal).
Place non-rotting recyclables in the blue bin and biodegradable waste in the green bin.

concepts.title: Vermicomposting
concepts.definition: A method of preparing high-quality compost using a specific type of earthworm called redworms to break down organic matter.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Using redworms to accelerate the decomposition of kitchen waste into manure.
question_patterns: what is vermicomposting
how are redworms used in making manure
describe the process of vermicomposting
which organism is known as the farmer's friend in composting

solution_steps.explain: Create a pit with a mesh or sand layer and add organic waste.
Add redworms to the pit and cover loosely with a cloth or grass.
Provide moisture and suitable food (no salt/oil/meat) for the worms.

concepts.title: Redworm Digestion and Gizzard
concepts.definition: Redworms lack teeth and use a specialized internal structure called a gizzard to grind their food, often aided by grit like eggshells.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Mechanical breakdown of food in redworms using a gizzard and supplemental grit.
question_patterns: how do redworms grind their food
what is a gizzard
why are eggshells added to a vermicompost pit
do redworms have teeth

solution_steps.explain: Redworms take in organic waste along with grit like powdered eggshells.
The gizzard uses the grit to mechanically grind the food into smaller particles.

concepts.title: Redworm Food Consumption
concepts.definition: The daily intake of food by redworms, which is approximately equal to their own body weight.
concepts.key_idea: Redworms consume their own weight in organic waste every day.
question_patterns: how much food can a redworm eat in a day
calculate the amount of waste consumed by redworms
if you have a certain weight of worms, how much food do they need daily

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the average weight of one worm by the total number of worms to find the total food capacity.

concepts.title: Redworm Population Growth
concepts.definition: Under favorable conditions of moisture and temperature, the population of redworms in a compost pit doubles every month.
concepts.key_idea: Exponential growth of redworms in a healthy composting environment.
question_patterns: how fast do redworms multiply
calculate the number of redworms after a few months
how many worms will be in the pit if the population doubles every month

solution_steps.explain: The population doubles for every month passed.

concepts.title: City Garbage Estimation
concepts.definition: A method to estimate the total volume of waste produced by a city based on individual household generation rates.
concepts.key_idea: Scaling household waste data to estimate large-scale urban garbage generation.
question_patterns: how to estimate the garbage generated by a city
calculate the number of buckets of waste produced by a town daily
estimate city waste based on family garbage data

solution_steps.explain: Divide the number of buckets by the days it took to fill them.
Divide the daily family waste by the number of family members.
Multiply the per person waste by the total city population.

concepts.title: Recycling Paper
concepts.definition: In brief, the action of converting discarded paper into new usable sheets by creating a pulp and drying it on a mesh.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Reducing waste by processing old paper into new handmade paper products.
question_patterns: how can we recycle paper at home
describe the steps to make recycled paper
what materials are needed for paper recycling
can all types of paper be recycled

solution_steps.explain: Tear paper into pieces, soak in water for a day, and pound into a thick paste.
Spread the paste uniformly on a wire mesh frame and drain the water.
Remove the wet layer and dry it in the sun to form a new sheet.

concepts.title: Plastic Waste Hazards
concepts.definition: The environmental and health dangers caused by the excessive use and improper disposal of non-biodegradable plastics.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Plastics do not rot and release toxic gases when heated or burnt.
question_patterns: why is plastic a problem for the environment
what happens when plastics are burnt
how do plastic bags affect stray animals and drainage systems
list ways to minimize the use of plastics

solution_steps.explain: Recognize that plastics do not decompose naturally in soil.
Note that burning plastics releases harmful gases that can cause diseases like cancer.
Observe how plastic waste chokes drains and harms animals that swallow it.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If a redworm weighs {worm_weight} grams and you have {worm_count} worms in your pit, how much food can they eat in a day?

solution_template.explain: Total food consumed is the weight of one worm times the number of worms.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A family of {members} fills {buckets} buckets of garbage in {days} days. If a town has a population of {population}, estimate the total daily garbage buckets generated.

solution_template.explain: Divide buckets by days to get daily family generation.
Divide daily family waste by family members.
Multiply per person waste by city population.
